transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve gotten really scared of seeing rats. I work cleaning buildings, and it’s gotten to where I can’t do parts of my job anymore, especially around trash rooms or older areas. I know in my head it’s probably not really dangerous, but the thought of seeing one just… stops me.
When you think about seeing a rat, do you ever feel like you're going to have a panic attack?

Yes. If I hear scratching near a wall or see something move by a pipe, my body reacts right away. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I just feel like I have to get out of there before I can even think straight.
Are you afraid of other animals or situations that might be similar to seeing rats, like mice or other small creatures?

It’s mainly rats. The thought of seeing one is what really gets to me. Like at work, if I’m near a trash room or an old part of a building, I start worrying there might be one, and it’s bad enough that I avoid doing parts of the job. I know it’s probably not really dangerous, but I still can’t handle it.
Is it the thought of the rat itself that scares you, or is it more about where the rat might be, like in a dirty or dark place?

It’s really the rat itself. I mean, the dark or dirty places make me nervous because that’s where I think I might see one, like trash rooms or old parts of buildings. But the main thing is the thought of a rat showing up. Even when I know it’s probably not actually dangerous, I just can’t deal with it, and it’s gotten in the way of my cleaning work.
Have you ever had a strong fear reaction to something that resembles a rat, but isn't actually a rat?

Yes, if it’s something that makes me think it could be a rat. Like if I hear scratching in a wall, or see something move near a pipe, I react before I even know what it is. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I just feel like I need to get out of there right away.
Does your fear reaction happen only when you think you might see a rat, or does it also happen when you see pictures or videos of rats?

It happens when I think one might be there, yes. Like if I hear scratching near a wall or see something move by a pipe, my body reacts right away—my heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I feel like I have to get out before I can even think straight.
Does seeing pictures or videos of rats trigger your fear reaction?

Pictures or videos can bother me some, but it’s not like when I think one might actually be there. If I hear scratching in a wall or see something move by a pipe, my body reacts right away—my heart pounds, my hands shake, and I feel like I need to get out before I can think straight.
Does your fear of rats also extend to similar animals like mice when you encounter them in real life?

It’s mostly rats that I’m scared of. If I thought a mouse was a rat, or it was in the same kind of place like a trash room, I’d probably react. But what’s really gotten bad is the thought of seeing a rat at work—it’s to the point I can’t do parts of my cleaning job anymore, even when I know it’s probably just an old building and not really dangerous.
Does your fear of rats occur immediately upon seeing a rat, or can it be triggered by just being in a place where rats might be?

It can happen just being somewhere I think rats might be. If I hear scratching by a wall or see something move near a pipe, I react right away—my heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I feel like I need to get out before I can even think.
Does thinking about possibly seeing a rat in any location, not just at work, trigger your fear reaction?

Yes, it can. It’s not only at work, but work is where it’s gotten the worst because I’m cleaning old areas or trash rooms. Just thinking I might see a rat can make me want to avoid that place, even though I know it probably isn’t really dangerous.
Is your fear of rats triggered by just thinking about rats in general, or is it more about thinking you might encounter one in a specific situation?

It’s more about thinking I might actually run into one in a place, especially at work. Like if I’m going into an old part of the building or a trash room, just the thought of seeing a rat there can stop me. It’s gotten bad enough that I can’t do some parts of my cleaning job, even though I know it’s probably not really dangerous.
Is your fear of rats ever triggered by thinking about being in a dirty or dark place, even if you don't think a rat is actually there?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it just from a place being dirty or dark by itself. It’s more when my mind goes to, “what if there’s a rat in here?” Then I start reacting.
Does your fear reaction happen with other animals that are not rats but might resemble them in some way?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it with other animals, at least not in the same way. It’s mostly rats that set me off.
Does your fear reaction to rats also happen with other objects or situations that are not rats but might remind you of them?

I don’t think so. I mean, I can’t really name any object or situation besides actually thinking a rat might be there. It’s not like other things set me off the same way, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Is your fear reaction to rats ever triggered by something that is not a rat, but is related to rats in some other way, such as their habitat or droppings?

Yes. If I hear scratching near a wall, or see something move by a pipe, I react right away. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I feel like I need to get out before I can even think clearly.
Is there anything else besides rats or the thought of rats that triggers this fear reaction in you?

Yes, mostly things that make me think a rat might be right there. Like if I hear scratching near a wall, or I see something move by a pipe, I react right away. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I feel like I need to get out before I can even think straight.
Is your fear reaction ever triggered by something that you know is not a rat, but still causes you to think one might be present?

Yes. Even if I don’t actually see a rat, if I hear scratching near a wall or see something move by a pipe, I immediately think one might be there. My body just reacts—my heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I feel like I have to get away before I can think straight.
Is your fear of rats ever triggered by being in a situation or place where you think rats might be, even if you don't actually see one?

Yes. I avoid places where I think they might be—like basements, storage rooms, laundry areas, or alley dumpsters. If I have to clean one, I’ll keep the door open and try to get through it as fast as I can, but I’m scared the whole time.
Is your fear reaction ever triggered by something other than rats or the thought of rats being present?
I don’t think so. It’s mainly when I think there could be a rat around, or something reminds me of that. I haven’t noticed it happening from anything totally different.
